precepts.text: Aaron laid both hands on the scapegoat to put the sins upon it.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 goes on to “laying on of hands”, and Leviticus shows where that came from: “And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat”. That is what we did. The high priest laid his hands on the goat to put the sins of Israel upon it.

So Paul was saying: all that stuff the priests were doing, we have to leave it. Christ is the new high priest. The laying on of hands belongs with the animal sacrifice and the washings, the principles we leave to go on unto perfection.

precepts.text: The sin offering yields skins, as the Most High made coats of skins to cover sin.
precepts.point: The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.” The sin offering yields skins.

So when the Lord God made Adam and his wife “coats of skins”, an animal had been slain for sin. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice, and the skins that covered them came from a sacrifice for their sin.

precepts.text: The scapegoat is presented alive to make an atonement, standing in for the faults of others.
precepts.point: That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The blood required at the hand of every beast is the animal standing in for man. That is the scapegoat. “Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the Lord, and the other lot for the scapegoat.” The goat on which the Lord’s lot fell is offered “for a sin offering”, and the scapegoat “shall be presented alive before the Lord, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness.”

The scapegoat takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is what the coats of skins were for Adam and Eve, and what Cain and Abel knew when they brought their offerings: the judgment for sin has always been death, and the animal stands in the sinner’s place.

precepts.text: On the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest makes an atonement to cleanse the children of Israel from all their sins, an everlasting statute.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
Aaron made atonement upon the horns of the incense altar “once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements”. This altar served the day of atonement, and Leviticus 16 lays that day out.

“And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all”. On that day the priest made an atonement “for the holy sanctuary”, “for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar”, and “for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation”, “to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord.”

“And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year.” Once a year: that is the once in a year of Exodus 30:10.

precepts.text: A statute for ever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day, ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest made an atonement to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
The tenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a large gathering, wherein “ye shall afflict your souls: ye shall not do any work therein.” This is the day of atonement, and Leviticus 16 institutes it.

“And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord.”

A statute for ever: on that day the priest made an atonement to cleanse the people from all their sins before the Lord. “It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever.” That is the sin offering of atonement the offerings of Numbers 29 are laid beside.

precepts.text: The LORD said Aaron must not come at all times into the holy place before the mercy seat, that he die not.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not.”

Only chosen men could come near the ark. The Lord set many stipulations upon it, even after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire. Even Aaron, the high priest, could not come before the mercy seat at all times, lest he die. The Most High is holy and not to be handled carelessly.

So when the oxen shook the cart and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error.” Grabbing it was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared the ark holy and untouchable.

precepts.text: Aaron must put on the holy linen coat and garments and wash his flesh before coming into the holy place.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
Before Aaron could come into the holy place, “He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on.”

Everything in that day had to be done to a T. If the high priest had to be washed and clothed in holy garments before coming near the mercy seat, Uzzah could not lay his hand on the ark at the threshingfloor. The Lord was not playing about his commandments.

We owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ.

precepts.text: After the death of Aaron's two sons the Lord charges that Aaron come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, lest he die, and that when he comes he must bring a bullock and a ram, wash his flesh in water, and put on the holy linen garments, showing that entrance into the holy place was not to be taken lightly.
precepts.point: The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount, the cherubims, the ark, the altar of incense, and all its parts.

note.label: 1 Kings 6: Building the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died”. He charged “that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.”

When Aaron came, he had to come “with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering”, put on “the holy linen coat”, the linen breeches, girdle and mitre, “these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on.” Entrance into the holy place was not to be taken lightly.

The pattern of the house was not invented by Solomon. The Most High had already shown the fashion of the sanctuary to Moses in the mount: the holy place within the vail, the mercy seat upon the ark, and all its parts. Solomon spent seven years building the house “according to all the fashion of it”, the fashion the Most High had given.
